title: Design a Deck of Cards and a Card Game (OOD)
prompt: Design a deck of cards that you can shuffle and deal from, then show how you would build a generic card game (say Blackjack) on top of it. Model the classes — Card, Deck, Player, Game — their relationships, and the key methods. Sketch the class diagram.
blurb: The OOD fundamentals check — clean Card/Deck modeling, a correct shuffle, and a game layered on top without hard-coding one game's rules.

rubric.label: Requirements clarification
rubric.description: Asks whether it's a generic deck or a specific game, how many players, jokers, multiple decks, and what 'deal' means before coding.

rubric.label: Core entities
rubric.description: Identifies Card, Suit/Rank (enums), Deck, Hand, Player, and a Game abstraction.

rubric.label: Class design
rubric.description: Card immutable with Suit+Rank enums (not magic ints/strings), Deck owns the list and deal/shuffle, Hand separate from Player.

rubric.label: Relationships
rubric.description: Deck composes Cards, Player has-a Hand, Game aggregates Players and a Deck; correct ownership/multiplicity.

rubric.label: API methods
rubric.description: shuffle(), deal(n)/dealCard(), Hand.add/value; sensible return types and empty-deck handling.

rubric.label: Design patterns
rubric.description: Strategy or Template Method to make the Game generic; Factory for deck construction; each justified, not forced.

rubric.label: Extensibility
rubric.description: A different game (Poker) or variant (jokers, multiple decks, custom scoring) reuses Card/Deck without changes.

rubric.label: SOLID principles
rubric.description: Single-responsibility (Deck deals, Game rules, Hand scores) and open/closed for new games/scoring.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: Dealing from an empty deck, reshuffle, duplicate-card prevention, uniform shuffle correctness.

rubric.label: Communication
rubric.description: Explains the shuffle algorithm, separates deck mechanics from game rules, and reasons about the generic-game boundary.

functional_requirements: Represent a standard 52-card deck of unique Cards (Suit + Rank)
Shuffle the deck uniformly at random
Deal cards from the top of the deck to hands/players
Represent a player's Hand and compute its value for a game
Support building a concrete game (e.g., Blackjack) with its own rules on the shared deck
nonfunctional_requirements: Cards immutable and unique — no duplicates dealt
Deck reusable across different games (generic design)
Easy to add new games or variants without touching Card/Deck
clarifying_questions: Generic deck only, or a specific game like Blackjack? How many players?
Standard 52 cards, or jokers / multiple decks (as in casino Blackjack shoes)?
Does 'deal' remove cards from the deck, and do we reshuffle when it runs low?
Is Ace high, low, or both (game-dependent)?
Do we need a discard pile / return cards to the deck?

core_classes.name: Card
core_classes.responsibility: Immutable value object: a Suit and a Rank; knows its game-agnostic identity, not its point value.

core_classes.name: Rank (enum)
core_classes.responsibility: TWO..TEN, JACK, QUEEN, KING, ACE — may carry a default nominal value, but game-specific scoring lives in the game.

core_classes.name: Deck
core_classes.responsibility: Owns an ordered list of Cards; shuffles and deals from the top; tracks remaining cards.

core_classes.name: Hand
core_classes.responsibility: A collection of cards held by a player; can be scored by a game's rules.

core_classes.name: Player
core_classes.responsibility: A participant with a Hand (and, for gambling games, a balance).

core_classes.name: Game (abstract) / BlackjackGame
core_classes.responsibility: Orchestrates a round: deals, applies game-specific rules and scoring, decides the winner. Template Method for the round flow.

core_classes.name: ScoringStrategy (interface, optional)
core_classes.responsibility: Pluggable per-game card valuation (Blackjack vs Poker).

relationships: Deck composes Card (1..52) — cards are created and owned by the deck
Player has-a Hand (composition); Hand aggregates Cards
Game aggregates Players (2..*) and has-a Deck
BlackjackGame extends Game (inheritance / Template Method for round flow)
Suit and Rank are enums referenced by Card

design_patterns.where: Game.playRound() defines the round skeleton; subclasses fill in deal/score/decide-winner
design_patterns.why: Reuse the round flow across games while varying the rules.
Different games score the same cards differently without editing Deck or Card.

design_patterns.where: DeckFactory building a standard 52, a jokers deck, or a multi-deck shoe
design_patterns.why: Vary deck composition without callers knowing the details.

apis: Card dealCard() — throws/empty-signals when deck exhausted
state_transitions: Deck: FULL/ORDERED --shuffle--> SHUFFLED --dealCard * k--> PARTIALLY_DEALT --remaining()==0--> EMPTY --reset--> FULL
Blackjack player turn (optional): BETTING --> DEALT --> HIT/STAND --> BUST/STAND (resolved)
edge_cases: Dealing from an empty deck — throw or return Optional, don't return null silently
Reshuffle / reset when the shoe runs low
No duplicate cards — deck constructed once from the enum cross-product
Shuffle bias — must use Fisher-Yates, not sort-by-random or naive swaps
Ace dual value in Blackjack scoring (1 or 11) handled in the game, not in Card
concurrency: Typically single-threaded (turn-based) — call out that a real multiplayer server would serialize turns and guard the deck
If multiple players deal concurrently, synchronize dealCard so no two players get the same physical card
extensibility: New game (Poker, Hearts): new Game subclass + ScoringStrategy, reusing Card/Deck/Hand unchanged
Jokers or multiple decks: a DeckFactory variant; Card gains a JOKER rank if needed
Custom scoring / house rules: swap the ScoringStrategy
Discard pile / draw-and-return: add a discard collection the game manages

deep_dives.probe: How exactly do you shuffle? Why is Fisher-Yates uniform and why is sorting by a random key or repeated random swaps biased?
Where does a card's point value live — on Card, on Rank, or in the game? Why does putting Blackjack's Ace=1/11 on Card hurt reuse?
How do you make Game reusable for Poker without editing Blackjack — Template Method skeleton plus a scoring Strategy?

followup_bank.question: Walk me through the exact shuffle algorithm — is it Fisher-Yates? Why not Collections.shuffle-by-random-sort or naive swaps?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions value or points or score
followup_bank.question: Should the point value live on the Card or in the game? What breaks if Card knows Blackjack's Ace rule?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions int or string for suit or rank
followup_bank.question: Why enums for Suit and Rank instead of ints/strings — what safety and iteration benefits do you get?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions blackjack or poker or game
followup_bank.question: How do you share the round flow across games — Template Method — while letting each game score differently?

tradeoffs: Value on Rank (convenient) vs value in Game/Strategy (reusable) — keep game-specific scoring out of Card
Single Deck class parameterized by a factory (flexible) vs subclasses per deck type (explicit)
Template Method (shared skeleton, inheritance coupling) vs full Strategy composition (looser, more objects)
reference.reference_answer: A strong junior answer models Card as an immutable value object over Suit and Rank enums (never magic ints/strings), keeps game-specific point values out of Card, and gives Deck ownership of the card list with a correct Fisher-Yates shuffle and top-deal that signals cleanly on exhaustion. Player has-a Hand; Hand aggregates Cards. The generic-game layer uses a Template Method Game whose playRound skeleton is filled by BlackjackGame, with scoring pulled into a Strategy so Poker or house variants reuse Card/Deck/Hand untouched. The candidate handles empty-deck, reshuffle, no-duplicates, and Ace dual-value (in the game, not the card), and can explain why Fisher-Yates is unbiased. Bonus for a DeckFactory covering jokers/multi-deck shoes.

interviewer_notes: This is a junior-level fundamentals check — reward clean enum use, an immutable Card, and correct separation of deck mechanics from game rules. The two probes that reveal depth: (1) the shuffle — make them state Fisher-Yates and explain why sort-by-random is biased; (2) where card value lives — if they put Blackjack's Ace=11 on the Card, ask what happens when they add Poker. Push the generic-game boundary (Template Method + scoring Strategy) but don't demand heavy patterns from a junior — forcing five patterns onto a deck of cards is itself the over-engineering trap to note. Check empty-deck handling (no silent null). If time remains, ask them to add jokers or a second game to test reuse.
